turns.en: The good news is that at this point, it knows me well enough and my blogs, and I've actually, it knows my weird sense of humor, so it's able to ape me pretty well. I'll just say, "I need a 250 word post on," like today, today's post was a post that ChatGPT helped me with it. I said, "I believe that there's a refrain that needs to happen with the soul. We tend to say, 'I have a soul, or I don't have a soul,' but what if my soul has me? What if in fact, my job is just to be this vehicle for my soul to go to the next lifetime?" (01:09:56): My job is to be this steward of the soul. I said, "Write me something around that." It was just a weird idea. Of course, not all my blog posts are so new age, and I like that. I write a lot on leadership, but that was one that within 30 seconds, I had a 250 word blog post that I then adapted, and there you go.
turns.zh: 好消息是，在这一点上，它足够了解我和我的博客，而且实际上，它知道我奇怪的幽默感，所以它能够很好地模仿我。我只会说，“我需要一篇 250 字的帖子”，就像今天一样，今天的帖子是 ChatGPT 帮助我完成的。我说：“我相信灵魂需要克制。我们倾向于说，‘我有灵魂，或者我没有灵魂’，但如果我的灵魂有我呢？如果事实上，我的工作只是成为我的灵魂去下一生的载体呢？” (01:09:56)：我的工作就是成为灵魂的管家。我说：“给我写一些关于这个的东西。”这只是一个奇怪的想法。当然，并非我所有的博客文章都是新时代的，我喜欢这一点。我写了很多关于领导力的文章，但那是在 30 秒内，我写了一篇 250 字的博客文章，然后我对其进行了改编，就这样了。

turns.zh: 惊人的。 Chip，我们已经介绍了很多内容。我们走过了你的一生。也许实际上只是冰山一角。至此，我们进入了非常激动人心的闪电回合。我有五个问题要问你。你准备好了吗？

turns.en: Yes. Let's do it.
turns.zh: 是的。我们开始做吧。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: First question, what are two or three books that you find yourself recommending most to other people?
turns.zh: 第一个问题，您发现自己最向其他人推荐的两三本书是什么？

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: My favorite book of all time, Man's Search for Meaning, Viktor Frankl in a concentration camp in World War II. When someone's going through a hard time in their life, I say, "Read that book. You'll realize it's not so bad, what you're going through." It also really speaks to this idea of despair equals suffering, minus meaning. I wrote a book called Emotional Equations that was a New York Times bestseller that spoke to this idea that what if you could take all of your emotions and turn them into equations? (01:11:04): Very engineering-minded of me. That's one. I love any book by Liz Gilbert, sort of the opposite. Elizabeth Gilbert wrote Eat, Pray, Love. Her book, she's on faculty at MEA. She teaches here. Big Magic is just a beautiful book about sort of how do you get in the flow to allow the genie to come through you. Her Ted Talk in 2009 was about the fact that genius is not about being the genius yourself. It's about being the receptacle for the genie to come through you.
turns.zh: 我一直以来最喜欢的一本书，《人类寻找意义》，维克托·弗兰克尔在二战集中营中的故事。当有人在生活中经历困难时期时，我会说：“读那本书。你会意识到你正在经历的事情并没有那么糟糕。”它也真正说明了这种想法：绝望等于痛苦，失去了意义。我写了一本名为《情感方程》的书，这本书是《纽约时报》的畅销书，其中谈到了这样一个想法：如果你可以将所有情绪转化为方程，会怎样？ (01:11:04)：我非常有工程头脑。这是一个。我喜欢莉兹·吉尔伯特的任何一本书，但恰恰相反。伊丽莎白·吉尔伯特写了《美食、祈祷和爱》。她的书，她是 MEA 的教员。她在这里教书。 《大魔法》是一本精美的书，讲述了如何进入流动状态，让精灵穿过你。她在 2009 年的 Ted Talk 讲的是这样一个事实：天才并不意味着你自己就是天才。这是关于成为精灵通过你而来的容器。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I want to come back to this equation you shared. I was going to get to it, but I didn't, so this is a good opportunity to. There's a couple that are really interesting to me. This is, you wrote about these in a book. You have a bunch of these equations about living a happier life. The one you shared is despair equals suffering, minus meaning.
turns.zh: 我想回到你分享的这个等式。我本想这么做，但我没有，所以这是一个很好的机会。有一对夫妇对我来说非常有趣。这是，你在一本书中写到了这些。你有一堆关于过上幸福生活的方程式。你分享的是绝望等于痛苦，失去了意义。

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: The implication there is if you want less despair, increase the meaning.
turns.zh: 这意味着如果你想要减少绝望，就增加意义。

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: That's right.
turns.zh: 这是正确的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Or reduce the suffering.
turns.zh: 或者减少痛苦。

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: Suffering, Buddhist philosophy, the first noble truth of Buddhism is that suffering is ever-present. If suffering's a constant and you have two variables, using some algebra, I guess, you know that if you have more meaning, you have less suffering. That's that one.
turns.zh: 苦，佛教哲学，佛教的第一圣谛是苦是无时不在的。如果痛苦是一个常数，而你有两个变量，使用一些代数，我想，你就会知道，如果你有更多的意义，你就会有更少的痛苦。就是那个。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: The other one that I love is anxiety equals uncertainty times powerlessness. Maybe talk about that one briefly.
turns.zh: 我喜欢的另一件事是焦虑等于不确定性乘以无力感。也许简单地谈谈这一点。

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: 98% of anxiety comes from two sources. One is what you don't know, and number two is what you can't control or influence, and based upon social science. You can create an anxiety balance sheet and create four columns. First column is what is it you do know about the thing that's making you anxious? The second column is, what is it you don't know? The third column is what is it you can control or influence? The fourth column is what is it you can't control or influence? (01:13:01): When you take free-floating anxiety and put it into an equation, it actually makes it more tangible, and you often are less anxious as a result.
turns.zh: 98%的焦虑有两个来源。一是你不知道的事情，二是你无法控制或影响的事情，并且基于社会科学。您可以创建焦虑资产负债表并创建四列。第一栏是您对让您焦虑的事情了解多少？第二栏是，你不知道什么？第三栏是你可以控制或影响什么？第四栏是你无法控制或影响的是什么？ (01:13:01)：当你将自由浮动的焦虑放入一个等式中时，实际上它会变得更加切实，结果你通常会不那么焦虑。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Boom. Okay, so if you're feeling anxious right now, this is an exercise you can do and you'll feel less anxious in like five minutes is what I'm hearing.
turns.zh: 繁荣。好吧，如果你现在感到焦虑，你可以做这个练习，据我所知，五分钟后你就会感觉不那么焦虑了。

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, excellent. Very, very good nugget of advice. Okay, let's keep going with the lightning round. Come back from our tangent. Do you have a favorite recent movie or TV show you've really enjoyed?
turns.zh: 好的，非常好。非常非常好的建议。好吧，让我们继续闪电回合。从我们的切线回来。您最近有最喜欢的电影或电视节目吗？

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: Ted Lasso is, I'm a sucker for that show. When it comes to movies, I'm a total movie buff. We have an annual MEA Film Festival at our Santa Fe campus. I would say that the film that I'm most excited about that is coming out that most people have never heard of, it's called I'll Push You. It's the story of two guys, one of whom is in a degenerative health condition and in a wheelchair, and his best friend pushes him the 500 miles of the Camino de Santiago, and it's the relationship they build along that way.
turns.zh: 特德·拉索是，我很喜欢那个节目。说到电影，我是个十足的电影迷。我们在圣达菲校区举办一年一度的 MEA 电影节。我想说的是，我最兴奋的电影即将上映，大多数人从未听说过，它的名字叫《我推你》。这是两个人的故事，其中一个人的健康状况不佳，坐在轮椅上，他最好的朋友推着他走完了 500 英里的圣地亚哥卡米诺之路，这是他们一路上建立的关系。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. Very deep cut. Do you have a favorite product that you recently discovered that you really love?
turns.zh: 惊人的。切口非常深。您最近发现自己真正喜欢的最喜欢的产品有吗？

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: Yes. Hair growing material. No. Do you know Viori shorts? I sound like Scott Galloway because he advertises this, but Viori shorts are like, I just love them. They're just breathe and they're comfortable.
turns.zh: 是的。生发材料。不，你知道 Viori 短裤吗？我听起来像斯科特·加洛韦（Scott Galloway），因为他做了广告，但维奥里短裤就像，我就是喜欢它们。他们只是呼吸并且很舒服。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm wearing Viori joggers right now. The one downside of Viori, not to make anyone mad, is they're kind of plasticky if you look at the material. I'm trying to like, I don't know, but I do love, there's nothing better. That's the problem. Anything else like this that is all cotton.
turns.zh: 我现在穿着 Viori 慢跑裤。 Viori 的一个缺点（不要让任何人生气）是，如果你看一下材料，它们有点塑料。我试着去喜欢，我不知道，但我确实爱，没有比这更好的了。这就是问题所在。像这样的其他东西都是纯棉的。

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm a fan. I have many Viori, I don't know if they're called joggers, just, I don't know, weekenders or something. Anyway, love you, Viori. Do you have a favorite life motto that you often come back to and find really useful in work or in life? I imagine you have many, but is there one that comes to mind?
turns.zh: 我是粉丝。我有很多 Viori，我不知道他们是否被称为慢跑者，只是，我不知道，周末者或其他什么。不管怎样，爱你，维奥里。您是否有一条最喜欢的人生格言，经常回想并发现它在工作或生活中非常有用？我想你可能有很多，但有哪一个是你想到的呢？

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: My favorite one right now is your painful life lessons are the raw material for your future wisdom. The premise of that is that wisdom often comes through the school of hard knocks. When you're in the midst of a really challenging time, you are developing your future wisdom that's going to be valuable to you.
turns.zh: 我现在最喜欢的一件事是你痛苦的人生教训是你未来智慧的原材料。其前提是，智慧往往来自于艰难的磨练。当你正处于一个真正具有挑战性的时刻时，你正在发展对你来说有价值的未来智慧。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, final question. You were on the board of Burning Man, or you still are?
turns.zh: 好的，最后一个问题。您曾经是火人节的董事会成员，还是现在仍然是？

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: I was.
turns.zh: 我是。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Was.
turns.zh: 曾是。

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: I helped found the board of Burning Man. Yeah.
turns.zh: 我帮助建立了火人节的董事会。是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. No big deal. I don't know if you know this, I got married at Burning Man. We had an unofficial wedding there on bicycles, so it's really meaningful to us. I've been there four or five times. What's something about Burning Man that maybe people don't know, some inside story or a really unexpected piece of the journey? I may imagine there's a lot, but what comes to mind?
turns.zh: 好的。没什么大不了的。我不知道你是否知道，我在火人节结婚了。我们骑着自行车在那里举行了一场非正式婚礼，所以这对我们来说真的很有意义。我已经去过四五次了。关于火人节，有哪些人们可能不知道的事情，一些内幕故事，还是旅程中真正意想不到的部分？我可能想象有很多，但我想到了什么？

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: I would say the best not well-known thing about Burning Man is that Burning Man own owns a place called Fly Ranch. Fly Ranch is about 10 miles from Burning Man. Now, when you go to the Burn, the event around Labor Day, you cannot go over there. It's locked off. It's 3,400 acres. If you look at Fly Ranch, FlyRanch.org, I think it might even be, or it's on the Burning Man site, Fly Ranch is the opposite of Burning Man. Burning Man is this alkaline desert. (01:16:29): There's no living life there at all. It's very masculine. Fly Ranch is porous, and lots of desert grasses, and hot springs, and hot pools, and birds, and wild horses, and it's one of my favorite hot springs places in the world. Just check it out, and you can go there when it's not during the event. It's quite beautiful.
turns.zh: 我想说关于火人节最好的不为人所知的事情是火人节拥有一个叫做飞翔牧场的地方。 Fly Ranch 距离火人节 (Burning Man) 约 10 英里。现在，当你去参加劳动节前后的“烧伤”活动时，你不能去那里。它被锁了。占地3,400英亩。如果你看看 Fly Ranch，FlyRanch.org，我想它甚至可能是，或者在火人节网站上，Fly Ranch 与火人节相反。火人节就是这片碱性沙漠。 (01:16:29)：那里根本没有生命。这是非常有男子气概的。飞蝇牧场是多孔的，有很多沙漠草、温泉、热水池、鸟类和野马，它是世界上我最喜欢的温泉地之一。看看吧，活动以外的时候也可以去。非常漂亮。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It feels like it might've inspired MEA in many ways.
turns.zh: 感觉它可能在很多方面给 MEA 带来了启发。

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: It did, yes.
turns.zh: 确实如此，是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Chip, two final questions. Where can folks find you online, and how can listeners be useful to you?
turns.zh: 奇普，最后两个问题。人们可以在网上哪里找到您？听众如何对您有用？

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: Online, MEAWisdom.com is the website for MEA. My website is ChipConley.com, C-O-N-L-E-Y, and I'm on LinkedIn. That's really, from a social media perspective, the thing that I do the most. I actually take my daily blogs and put them on LinkedIn. Then what your community can do, just come say hi, come check me out. If wisdom's interesting to you, and I think wisdom should be interesting to everybody here, on the MEA website, at the very bottom footer, you'll see a bunch of free resources. (01:17:43): One of them is called Why Successful Leaders Value Wisdom. It is a free resource, and there's also a free resource down there called The Anatomy of a Transition. Those two free resources, understanding how to build your TQ, your transitional intelligence, and understanding how to develop wisdom are two, to my mind, two of the most important modern skills that we can have.
turns.zh: MEAWisdom.com 是 MEA 的在线网站。我的网站是 ChipConley.com，C-O-N-L-E-Y，我的帐号是 LinkedIn。从社交媒体的角度来看，这确实是我做的最多的事情。事实上，我每天都会写博客并将它们放在 LinkedIn 上。那么你的社区可以做什么，只是来打个招呼，来看看我。如果你对智慧感兴趣，而且我认为这里的每个人都应该对智慧感兴趣，在 MEA 网站的最底部页脚处，你会看到一堆免费资源。 (01:17:43)：其中之一名为“为什么成功的领导者重视智慧”。它是一个免费资源，而且还有一个免费资源，名为“转型剖析”。在我看来，这两个免费资源，了解如何建立你的 TQ、你的过渡性智力，以及了解如何发展智慧，是我们可以拥有的两项最重要的现代技能。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It's funny when you say you're on LinkedIn. It doesn't resonate with me. Chip Conley on LinkedIn, posting on LinkedIn, something about...
turns.zh: 当你说你在 LinkedIn 上时，这很有趣。它没有引起我的共鸣。奇普·康利 (Chip Conley) 在 LinkedIn 上发布了有关...

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: I don't know. Why? Because I'm a little too Burning Man?
turns.zh: 我不知道。为什么？因为我有点太火人节了？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You're just, yeah, exactly. It feels like that's not your vibe, but I love that you do it, because that's where the people are.
turns.zh: 你只是，是的，完全正确。感觉这不是你的氛围，但我喜欢你这样做，因为那就是人们所在的地方。

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: Oh, I put wild, weird stuff up on LinkedIn, and thank God somebody's doing that.
turns.zh: 噢，我在 LinkedIn 上发布了一些疯狂、奇怪的东西，感谢上帝有人这么做了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: For some reason, I don't see it. I need to fix that. Chip, this was incredible. Everything I was hoping it'd be, thank you so much for being here and for sharing-
turns.zh: 由于某种原因，我没有看到它。我需要解决这个问题。奇普，这太不可思议了。一切都是我所希望的，非常感谢您来到这里并分享-

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: Thank you, Lenny.
turns.zh: 谢谢你，莱尼。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: ... your wisdom.
turns.zh: ...你的智慧。

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: I am so proud as I go back, like have your proud Papa who just loves to see you in your element, and I just want to make sure everybody knows the following. Lenny was so good to work with. Whenever you were assigned to a project as a PM, I appreciated it because I just knew that we were going to have great conversations. You're just an interesting dude.
turns.zh: 当我回去时，我感到非常自豪，就像你骄傲的爸爸一样，他喜欢看到你处于自己的状态，我只是想确保每个人都知道以下内容。和莱尼一起工作真是太好了。每当你被分配到一个项目作为产品经理时，我都会很感激，因为我知道我们将会进行愉快的对话。你只是一个有趣的家伙。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Well, I appreciate that, Chip. That's going to be the beginning of this whole episode. We're just going to put that up front. Just kidding. That was awesome, Chip. Really appreciate it.
turns.zh: 嗯，我很感激，奇普。这将是整个情节的开始。我们只是把它放在前面。只是在开玩笑。太棒了，奇普。真的很感激。

turns.speaker: Chip Conley
turns.en: Thanks.
turns.zh: 谢谢。
